answer: A durable defence is a bonded work history: every agent must lock a stake and build a verifiable record of useful, attested tasks before it can earn. Think of the stake as a jade seal — costly to forge, cheap to check — while each completed job acts as a beacon broadcasting that the agent did real work, not just spun up a copy. Sybil identities face basalt-hard economics: cloning an identity means re-paying the stake and re-doing the work from zero, so faking a thousand agents costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents amortise one stake over a long earning life.
